planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Alocasia scalprum is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, allowing the top inch or two to dry before watering again. Alocasia scalprum produces narrow, elongated, arrow-shaped leaves with a distinctly bullate (blistered or puckered) dark green surface and sunken venation, a rougher, more three-dimensional texture than the smoother, broader leaves of many other alocasia species. Its narrower leaf silhouette gives it a more slender, upright profile than wide-leaved alocasias, useful for a narrower bright spot. Keep it warm and humid, out of direct sun, which can scorch the leaf surface, and avoid overwatering, since textured-leaf alocasia species are often especially prone to root and stem rot in soggy mix.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, allowing the top inch or two to dry before watering again. Alocasia azlanii is a striking Malaysian species with narrow, pointed leaves in a deep coppery bronze-red overlaid with a network of raised, metallic-looking veins, giving the foliage an almost hammered-metal texture and warm color unlike the greens, silvers, or blacks of most other alocasia species. Its compact size and dramatic coloring have made it a highly sought-after collector's plant. Keep it warm and humid, out of direct sun, which can scorch the leaf surface, and avoid overwatering, since this species is especially prone to rot in soggy mix; a chunky, fast-draining aroid substrate is essential.

planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Alocasia venusta is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, allowing the top inch or two to dry before watering again. Alocasia venusta produces broad, arrow-shaped leaves with a soft, velvety surface in a warm coppery-red to bronze-green color, sometimes flushed with a subtle purplish sheen depending on light exposure, distinguishing it from the cooler silver or grey tones of many other collector alocasias. Its warm coloring and velvety texture make it a striking contrast plant alongside silver or dark-leaved alocasia species in a mixed collection. Keep it warm and humid, out of direct sun, which can scorch the leaf surface, and avoid overwatering, since alocasia species in general are prone to root and stem rot in soggy mix.
